observations: OBSERVATION 1, not charged. Header lines 14-15 write '5 unlabeled observations strings with no id member'. The register attaches 'with no id member' / 'with no id field' to OBJECTS - 'observationsNotFindings objects with no id member' (D-333 lineage, COORD line 19431), '2 attacksNotChargedWithDisclosure objects with no id field' (D-318), 'MUST-FIX findings with no id member' (six instances) - and never to strings. All twenty-four recorded 'N unlabeled X strings' recitations, including D-339's '4 unlabeled observations strings' and D-341's, stop at 'strings'. A JSON string has no members at all, so predicating the absence of an id member of one leans on the object frame that the word 'strings' simultaneously denies. Not charged, for four reasons that together put it below the SHOULD-FIX line: the claim is byte-true, not merely arguable - $.observations is five strings and there is no id anywhere; the dispatch itself mandates these exact words under 'Turn-1 Stage B return shapes (cite these; do not flatten)', so citing them is compliance, unlike turn-1 SF-1 where the dispatch-propagated tuple was byte-FALSE and had to be charged against the bytes; 'unlabeled' already carries the no-identifier meaning, so the clause is redundant rather than misleading; and it is cured in the entry's own second recitation at lines 113-114, which reads 'Claude Stage B turn-1 returned 5 unlabeled observations strings' with no such clause and is the form the operative text uses. The CLAUDE-CMLJ-V12-A1 test - whether another binding site makes the reader whole - is met here and was not met by turn-1 SF-1. Worth recording so a later entry reciting this cycle drops the clause rather than propagating it.

OBSERVATION 2, not charged. The Claude row of the 'Stage A observation disposition' table ends with 'SF-1 is landed: the four objects are not recited as sharing one exhaustive member tuple'. SF-1 is a Stage B turn-1 identifier, and the row it sits in is a Stage A row whose own Identifiers cell lists only D01-D04. Read in isolation the cell could be taken to attribute SF-1 to Stage A. Not charged: the identifier inventory is correct, since SF-1 is absent from the Identifiers cell where a mis-attribution would actually bind; and the stage is given explicitly at the three other sites that carry the same claim - line 12 ('Claude 2 Stage B turn-1'), line 112 ('Claude Stage B turn-1 identifier SF-1 is landed') and Decision line 171 (the same sentence). The register's own habit is to state landings in prose, as D-320 did ('The unlabeled Codex turn-1 SHOULD-FIX is landed'), so a later entry would naturally carry the prose form rather than the cell.

OBSERVATION 3, disclosure of a coverage gap this review could not close. The operator instruction for this turn was stricter than turn 1: 'Do not read any Codex review'. Turn 1 read the Codex Stage A bytes and certified the draft's Codex Stage A row against them. This turn did not open any Codex file; the draft's Codex Stage A row (line 106) and its newly added Codex Stage B turn-1 recitation (lines 16-21) were checked only against the dispatch's own return-shape blocks, which they match clause for clause and in order, and against the four Codex digests, which all reproduce. The Codex Stage A row is nonetheless well supported, because turn 1 verified the identical text against those bytes and the file's digest is unchanged. The Codex Stage B turn-1 recitation is new in this draft and no reading of this review has measured it against bytes. It is recorded here so the coordinator knows which single recitation in the entry rests on the dispatch rather than on a byte check by this reviewer.

OBSERVATION 4, not charged, carried forward unchanged from turn 1. The reversibility list omits D-086, which the dual-CONSENTed sibling D-339 carries in the same position. D-086 is the general gate-naming decision; the G29 naming decision is D-157, which the entry does name, and file 08's condition-4 row records G29 named under D-157. A 'does not unwrite' list is not asserted as exhaustive, and the entry makes no naming-parent claim that D-086 would have to bind. Turn 2 changed nothing here, so nothing new is charged.

OBSERVATION 5, verified and worth recording. The draft's answer to OQ-G29-2 is not merely permitted, it is the condition D-320 attached. g29-fixture-corpus.v2 $.basedOn.leftoverJoinV6.role records leftover-join.v6 of G29's own proposedLaterWork as 'a later leftover-design cycle may author those copies only after OQ-G29-2 is answered', and g29-fixture-corpus.v1 left the question explicitly open ('which occupancy a later per-platform copy version would quote for the four D-002 platform tokens is not decided here'). The quotation from G10 occupancy v2, ORDERED-EQUAL against G23 occupancy v2, discharges that precondition without touching leftover-join.v6 of G29, which is exactly the division of authority the entry claims for itself.
reviewSummary: Thirty-seven attacks run - the seventeen the dispatch names and twenty added by this reviewer. Thirty-five refuted. Two sustained as wording observations and neither charged: an object-frame qualifier applied to strings that the dispatch itself mandates and that the entry's own second recitation already drops, and a stage-unqualified 'SF-1 is landed' inside a Stage A table cell that three other sites, including the operative Decision, state with its stage. Turn-1 SF-1 is landed exactly: the flattened member tuple is replaced by two tuples that reproduce the pinned Claude Stage A review's bytes in document order, and the correction appears in the operative Decision as well as the table, which the turn-1 draft did not do. All ten pinned digests reproduce; the subject and the frozen turn-1 draft are unmoved at 0444; COORD, file 08 and HEAD are unchanged. The forty fixture copies exist and are byte-identical to the ten D-318 implementations across four platform directories. The four D-002 platform tokens are quoted, not invented, and are ORDERED-EQUAL between G10 and G23 occupancy v2, discharging the precondition leftover-join.v6 of G29 attached to OQ-G29-2 without remasuring it. No row is marked SATISFIED, leftover-design of OBL-G29-FX-AUTHORING is left open on leftover-join.v6 of G29, staleness of the forty copies is deferred to a later leftover-join remasurement, and D-319 is treated as unrecorded throughout. One coverage limit is disclosed rather than hidden: by operator instruction no Codex review was opened this turn, so the newly added Codex Stage B turn-1 recitation was checked against the dispatch's return-shape block and the file's digest, not against its bytes.
decision: CONSENT - 0 MUST-FIX, 0 SHOULD-FIX. Thirty-seven attacks run, thirty-five refuted, two sustained as uncharged observations.
